import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# $a(n) = n$ if $n$ is prime, otherwise $a(n) = 1$

*References:*
- [A089026](https://oeis.org/A089026)
-/

namespace OeisA89026

/-- $a(n) = n$ if $n$ is a prime, otherwise $a(n) = 1$. -/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if n.Prime then n else 1

/-- Term theorems verifying the first few values of the sequence against the official OEIS b-file -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 2 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 3 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 1 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_5 : a 5 = 5 := by decide

end OeisA89026

review.notes: Checked all seven declarations: OeisA89026.a and a_0 through a_5. The definition matches the OEIS rule exactly, and Nat.prime_def confirms the conventional meaning of primality. Scratch Lean checks compiled successfully; evaluation matched all 5,000 official b-file rows, and none of the six theorem proofs depends on sorryAx. OEIS starts at index 1, so a_0 is an additional, harmless boundary test of the same defining rule—not a tabulated b-file term. All theorems are appropriately tagged category test; there are no answer slots or research-status claims to correct.
